headline: Your CloudLeap waterfall journey.
subheadline: One routed cascade that finds ERP-run shippers still paying for manual, carrier-by-carrier shipping, and hands each one the Piyovi proof that fits.
productSummary: CloudLeap (formerly Piyovi LLC; the platform is still called Piyovi) sells cloud multi-carrier shipping software for ERP-driven shippers: rate shopping, packing, labels and BOLs, shipment booking, spot quotes, tracking, invoice audit, DG and export compliance, across hundreds of parcel and LTL carriers, with pre-built connectors for Infor, SAP, Oracle, Microsoft Dynamics, Epicor, Sage, Acumatica, IFS and more. SOC 2 Type II compliant (cloudleap.com).
coreInsight: Every shipping tool says 'multi-carrier'. The shippers who will actually switch are the ones whose ERP is already on CloudLeap's connector list and who are visibly paying for the gap: hiring people to key shipments into WorldShip or FedEx Ship Manager, splitting parcel and LTL across tools, or bolting B2C orders onto a B2B shipping desk. Route on that cost, lead with Piyovi's customer proof, and let the catch-all carry every other supported-ERP shipper.

sections.label: Signal
sections.title: The signal is a supported ERP plus a visible manual-shipping cost
sections.takeaway: CloudLeap only wins where it has a pre-built ERP connector, so the ERP is the gate. Inside that gate, job posts, freight pages and storefront detection show how much the shipper is paying for disconnected, carrier-by-carrier shipping.

sections.label: Waterfall
sections.title: First match wins, top to bottom, catch-all underneath
sections.takeaway: Exclude existing CloudLeap customers, implementation partners and ERP vendors, then route: shipping job posts naming a desktop carrier tool, then parcel-plus-LTL shippers, then B2B shippers with a B2C storefront, then every other supported-ERP shipper. Each account lands in exactly one campaign.

sections.label: Tiers
sections.title: Four tiers, hottest to broadest
sections.takeaway: Pain comes from the trigger (re-keying shipments, split parcel/LTL workflows, B2C order load). Value props and proof come straight from cloudleap.com: pre-built ERP connectors, hundreds of parcel and LTL carriers, invoice audit, click-and-ship, and named customer results.

sections.label: Campaigns
sections.title: One campaign per tier, one offer per campaign
sections.takeaway: Operations Managers, Shipping / Warehouse Managers and Supply Chain Directors get the throughput and cost angle. IT / ERP Managers get the connector and implementation angle on Day 7.

sections.label: Emails
sections.title: Three-touch sequences, notice line first
sections.takeaway: Day 0 names the observed trigger, Day 3 rotates the value prop in-thread, Day 7 is the no-call ask: reply yes and we send the sheet. Every proof line is quoted from cloudleap.com customer testimonials.

sections.label: Launch
sections.title: Pull, route, send, then scale or cut on reply math
sections.takeaway: Build the supported-ERP shipper TAM once, run the routing agent, launch tiers with at least ~1,500 contacts, and judge each on positive replies per send. Keep adding shippers; do not rebuild the strategy.

signalReasons: CloudLeap's pre-built connectors cover a specific ERP list, and ERP usage is reliably detectable from technographic data, job posts and ERP marketplace / user-group listings, so the gate is observable.

Shipping, warehouse and logistics job posts routinely name the tools the hire will use (UPS WorldShip, FedEx Ship Manager, the ERP), exposing manual, carrier-by-carrier shipping in the shipper's own words.

Freight / LTL pages, shipping policies and 'we ship via' carrier mentions on a shipper's site show whether it runs both parcel and LTL, which is exactly where one multi-mode platform replaces several.

A B2C storefront (Shopify, BigCommerce, Magento, ERP web store) on a B2B distributor or manufacturer is detectable with BuiltWith and signals the order-volume pain CloudLeap's click-and-ship proof addresses.

sources.name: Technographic data (HG Insights / Apollo technologies / BuiltWith) + ERP marketplace and user-group lists (Infor, Microsoft, Oracle, SAP, Epicor)
sources.delivers: TAM gate: shippers running an ERP on CloudLeap's connector list (erp_detected, erp_source).

sources.name: Indeed + LinkedIn Jobs scrape (last 60 days)
sources.delivers: Shipping clerk, shipping/receiving, warehouse, logistics coordinator roles and the tools named in the post (UPS WorldShip, FedEx Ship Manager, ERP). Routing signal for Tier 1.

sources.name: Company website scrape (freight / shipping policy / 'ship via' pages)
sources.delivers: Parcel and LTL usage plus named LTL carriers (ships_ltl, ltl_carrier_named). Routing signal for Tier 2.

sources.name: BuiltWith storefront detection
sources.delivers: Shopify / BigCommerce / Magento / WooCommerce or ERP web store on a B2B shipper (b2c_storefront_detected). Routing signal for Tier 3.

sources.name: Trade association and event exhibitor lists (e.g. HARDI, Infor Velocity Week, Community Summit, where CloudLeap exhibits per cloudleap.com/events)
sources.delivers: Extra distributor and manufacturer accounts on supported ERPs for the TAM pull.

sources.name: Apollo / LinkedIn Sales Navigator
sources.delivers: Verified contacts: Operations Manager, Shipping / Warehouse Manager, Supply Chain Director, IT / ERP Manager at each routed shipper.

routingRules.if: cloudleap_customer = true (named on cloudleap.com, e.g. SEA Wire & Cable, Kalsec, Countrywide Tire & Rubber, Wencor, Industrial Supply, Woodland Gourmet, Ahern, Functional Devices, or any CRM customer list CloudLeap provides)
routingRules.why: Already a CloudLeap / Piyovi customer. Route to account management, not cold outbound.

routingRules.if: cloudleap_partner = true (Tech Mahindra, PlutoCloud, TechWize, Trangile, Focus Softnet, Apex Systems, Doppio Group, Godlan, Crescent Financial, KJC Consulting Group, ASW Global Consulting, Guide Technologies, Fortude, SNS Global, ICCG, NSA Computer Exchange, Electric Innovative Solutions, Merino Consulting Services, The Copley Consulting Group) OR erp_vendor_or_consultancy = true
routingRules.why: Implementation and referral partners, ERP publishers and ERP consultancies are channel, not shippers.

routingRules.if: erp_detected NOT in CloudLeap connector list (Infor (LN, M3, SyteLine/CSI, CloudSuite Distribution, WMS), SAP (Business One, ByDesign, ECC, S/4HANA), Oracle (NetSuite, EBS, Fusion Cloud, OTM, JD Edwards), Microsoft Dynamics 365 (F&O, Business Central), Epicor (Kinetic, P21), Sage (Intacct, X3), Acumatica, IFS, Rubicon, IBM AS/400)
routingRules.why: No pre-built connector, so the core value prop does not apply.

routingRules.if: shipping_job_posted_60d = true AND shipping_tool_named in {UPS WorldShip, FedEx Ship Manager, other single-carrier desktop tool}
routingRules.why: The shipper is hiring people to run carrier-by-carrier tools next to the ERP. Strongest, most time-bound, costed pain.

routingRules.if: ELSE IF ships_ltl = true AND ships_parcel = true
routingRules.then: Tier 2: Parcel + LTL in one place
routingRules.why: Two modes usually means two workflows. Piyovi rates, books and tracks parcel and LTL from one platform and audits carrier invoices.

routingRules.then: Tier 3: B2C orders on a B2B shipping desk
routingRules.why: Consumer orders multiply small-parcel volume. Click-and-ship and per-order time savings are the proof.

routingRules.if: ELSE (every remaining shipper on a supported ERP)
routingRules.why: Covers 100% of the TAM. Broad connector, carrier-coverage and implementation angle, softest ask.

tiers.name: Tier 1
tiers.label: Desktop carrier tools
tiers.trigger: Supported-ERP shipper posted a shipping / warehouse / logistics role in the last 60 days that names UPS WorldShip, FedEx Ship Manager or another single-carrier desktop tool.
tiers.pain: They are adding headcount to key shipments carrier by carrier and copy tracking back into the ERP, because shipping is not connected to the order.
tiers.valueProp: Pre-built ERP connectors automate order flow, packing, shipping, ship confirmations and tracking; rate shopping compares ship methods by cost and delivery time across hundreds of parcel and LTL carriers (cloudleap.com).
tiers.magnet: Shipping-desk time sheet (shipper plugs in orders/day and minutes per shipment) + {{erp}}-to-Piyovi connector overview
tiers.dataSource: Indeed + LinkedIn Jobs scrape matched to technographic ERP detection
tiers.accounts: Estimate only; accumulate to ~1,500 contacts before launch

tiers.name: Tier 2
tiers.label: Parcel + LTL in one place
tiers.trigger: Supported-ERP shipper whose site shows both parcel and LTL / freight shipping (freight page, shipping policy, named LTL carriers), not matched by Tier 1.
tiers.pain: Parcel and LTL live in separate tools and portals, so nobody compares modes on each order and carrier billing errors go unchecked.
tiers.valueProp: One platform for parcel, LTL/TL, 3PL and brokers: rate shopping, spot quotes, BOLs, booking and pickups, tracking with POD, and carrier invoice audit. Ahern had 13.97% carrier failures identified and credited through Piyovi's reporting tools (cloudleap.com).
tiers.magnet: Parcel + LTL mode-mix sheet + carrier invoice audit checklist
tiers.dataSource: Website scrape for freight / LTL signals + technographic ERP detection

tiers.name: Tier 3
tiers.label: B2C orders on a B2B shipping desk
tiers.trigger: Supported-ERP B2B distributor or manufacturer with a detected B2C / e-commerce storefront, not matched by Tiers 1-2.
tiers.pain: Consumer orders pile small-parcel volume onto a desk built for B2B shipments, and each order takes manual clicks to rate, label and confirm.
tiers.valueProp: Click-and-ship, labels and documents generated instantly, eCommerce connectors, address validation for residential deliveries. Countrywide Tire & Rubber saved 2-3 minutes per B2C order and scaled without adding staff (cloudleap.com).
tiers.magnet: B2C order-time sheet (orders/day x minutes saved) + Countrywide Tire & Rubber story
tiers.dataSource: BuiltWith storefront detection + technographic ERP detection
tiers.replyDensity: Medium. Clear volume pain, no urgency trigger (estimate)

tiers.name: Tier 4
tiers.label: Catch-all: ERP-native multi-carrier shipping
tiers.trigger: Every remaining shipper on a CloudLeap-supported ERP (no desktop-tool job post, no parcel+LTL signal, no B2C storefront detected).
tiers.pain: Shipping still sits outside the ERP, so rates, labels and tracking are handled in separate systems with manual re-entry.
tiers.valueProp: Pre-built connectors for Infor, SAP, Oracle, Microsoft Dynamics, Epicor, Sage, Acumatica, IFS and more; hundreds of parcel and LTL carriers; white-glove implementation; simple, transparent pricing; SOC 2 Type II (cloudleap.com).

campaigns.name: WorldShip job post: connect shipping to {{erp}}
campaigns.strategy: Notice the {{job_title}} post on {{job_board}} that names {{shipping_tool}}, ask whether the hire is really about keying shipments outside {{erp}}, offer the shipping-desk time sheet. Ops / Shipping Manager first, IT / ERP Manager on Day 7.
campaigns.overview: Smallest, hottest tier. Refill weekly from job boards; launch once ~1,500 contacts accumulate, otherwise route new rows through Tier 4 copy.

campaigns.name: Parcel + LTL: one platform, audited invoices
campaigns.strategy: Reference the {{ltl_carrier}} freight shipping on their site, poke at parcel and LTL living in separate portals, offer the mode-mix sheet and invoice audit checklist backed by Ahern's 13.97% credited carrier failures.
campaigns.overview: Supply Chain Director / Transportation Manager is the buyer. A/B cost (invoice audit) vs speed (one workflow).

campaigns.name: B2C storefront: click-and-ship
campaigns.strategy: Name the {{storefront}} store, ask how B2C orders get rated and labelled today, offer the order-time sheet with Countrywide Tire & Rubber's 2-3 minutes per order.
campaigns.overview: Ops / E-commerce Manager is the buyer. Good bridge from B2B shipping to consumer volume.

campaigns.name: Catch-all: shipping inside {{erp}}
campaigns.strategy: Billboard opener on ERP-native multi-carrier shipping for {{erp}} shippers, backed by Ahern (50%+ faster processing, live within one month), soft resource CTA.
campaigns.overview: Guarantees 100% TAM coverage. Winners here get promoted into ERP-specific variants (e.g. Infor vs Dynamics).

launchPlan: Pull the TAM: shippers (distributors, manufacturers, wholesalers) running an ERP on CloudLeap's connector list, from technographic data plus ERP marketplace, user-group and event exhibitor lists.
Apply exclusions first: CloudLeap / Piyovi customers (site logos plus any customer list CloudLeap shares), implementation and referral partners, ERP publishers and ERP consultancies.
Enrich once: 60-day job-board scrape for shipping roles and named tools, website scrape for parcel / LTL signals and named carriers, BuiltWith storefront detection.
Run the routing agent top to bottom: exclusions, Tier 1, Tier 2, Tier 3, catch-all. Assert every account exits with exactly one tier.
Find contacts via Apollo / Sales Navigator: Operations or Shipping Manager first, Supply Chain Director second, IT / ERP Manager for the Day 7 'you or {{alt_decision_maker}}' line.
Have CloudLeap approve the four offers (time sheet, mode-mix sheet, B2C order-time sheet, ERP one-pager) and every proof line before sends start.

Launch only tiers with ~1,500+ contacts. Tier 1 accumulates weekly; until it clears ~1,500, send those rows through Tier 4 copy. Review reply math after 1,500 sends, scale or cut, keep adding shippers.

thresholds.rate: Worse than 1 / 500, or <1% reply after 1,500 sends
thresholds.action: Cut the tier and re-route its leads to the catch-all
